question: What does the Linux kernel do for an EPOLLET (edge-triggered) registration, from a readiness change on the watched file to epoll_wait returning, and what do the official docs require of the caller? Find, in the man pages (epoll(7), epoll_ctl(2), epoll_wait(2)) and the kernel source (fs/eventpoll.c): when an event is queued on the ready list; what epoll_wait does with an edge-triggered item versus a level-triggered item after reporting it; whether new data arriving on a file not yet drained produces another report; the effect of EPOLL_CTL_MOD (re-arming); EPOLLONESHOT and EPOLLEXCLUSIVE combined with EPOLLET; behaviour across dup, fork and close; the non-blocking plus read-until-EAGAIN requirement and its exact wording; and the kernel versions each behaviour applies to.

sources.rank_basis: tier B: project's own home (Linux man-pages project repository, man/man2/epoll_wait.2 at tag man-pages-6.19; the COLOPHON of S2 names this repository as the project's)

facts.summary: An epoll instance holds an interest list and a ready list; the kernel fills the ready list as I/O activity happens on the registered file descriptors.
facts.quote: The ready list is dynamically populated by the kernel as a result of I/O activity on those file descriptors.

facts.summary: Edge-triggered mode delivers events only when the monitored file descriptor changes: one event per received chunk of data.
facts.quote: edge-triggered mode delivers events only when changes occur on the monitored file descriptor, that is, an event will be generated upon each receipt of a chunk of data.

facts.summary: In the pipe example (2 kB written, 1 kB read), a second epoll_wait on an EPOLLET registration will probably hang although data remains, because the partial read did not consume the buffer.
facts.quote: If the rfd file descriptor has been added to the epoll interface using the EPOLLET (edge-triggered) flag, the call to epoll_wait(2) done in step 5 will probably hang despite the available data still present in the file input buffer; … Since the read operation done in 4 does not consume the whole buffer data, the call to epoll_wait(2) done in step 5 might block indefinitely.

facts.summary: The page says an EPOLLET application should use nonblocking file descriptors, and gives the suggested use as nonblocking descriptors plus waiting for an event only after read or write returns EAGAIN.
facts.quote: An application that employs the EPOLLET flag should use nonblocking file descriptors to avoid having a blocking read or write starve a task that is handling multiple file descriptors. The suggested way to use epoll as an edge-triggered (EPOLLET) interface is as follows: (1) with nonblocking file descriptors; and (2) by waiting for an event only after read(2) or write(2) return EAGAIN.

facts.summary: Level-triggered is the default when EPOLLET is not given, and then epoll has the same semantics as poll(2).
facts.quote: By contrast, when used as a level-triggered interface (the default, when EPOLLET is not specified), epoll is simply a faster poll(2), and can be used wherever the latter is used since it shares the same semantics.

facts.summary: Even in edge-triggered mode several events can be generated by several chunks of data; EPOLLONESHOT disables the descriptor after one event, and the caller must re-arm it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.
facts.quote: Since even with edge-triggered epoll, multiple events can be generated upon receipt of multiple chunks of data, the caller has the option to specify the EPOLLONESHOT flag, to tell epoll to disable the associated file descriptor after the receipt of an event with epoll_wait(2). When the EPOLLONESHOT flag is specified, it is the caller's responsibility to rearm the file descriptor using epoll_ctl(2) with EPOLL_CTL_MOD.

facts.summary: When several threads, or processes that inherited the epoll fd across fork, wait on one epoll fd and an EPOLLET-marked descriptor becomes ready, only one of them is woken.
facts.quote: If multiple threads (or processes, if child processes have inherited the epoll file descriptor across fork(2)) are blocked in epoll_wait(2) waiting on the same epoll file descriptor and a file descriptor in the interest list that is marked for edge-triggered (EPOLLET) notification becomes ready, just one of the threads (or processes) is awoken from epoll_wait(2).

facts.summary: epoll(7) says that with EPOLLWAKEUP set the system stays awake from the moment the event is queued until the following epoll_wait call; it states no condition on EPOLLET.
facts.quote: When the EPOLLWAKEUP flag is set in the events field for a struct epoll_event, the system will be kept awake from the moment the event is queued, through the epoll_wait(2) call which returns the event until the subsequent epoll_wait(2) call.

facts.summary: The page's example uses each ready fd until read or write returns EAGAIN, and says an event-driven state machine should record its state after EAGAIN to resume later.
facts.quote: The function do_use_fd() uses the new ready file descriptor until EAGAIN is returned by either read(2) or write(2). An event-driven state machine application should, after having received EAGAIN, record its current state so that at the next call to do_use_fd() it will continue to read(2) or write(2) from where it stopped before.

facts.summary: An interest-list entry is keyed by the file descriptor number together with the open file description.
facts.quote: The key is the combination of the file descriptor number and the open file description

facts.summary: Registering the same fd twice probably gives EEXIST, but a dup'ed fd can be added to the same epoll instance, for example with a different event mask.
facts.quote: You will probably get EEXIST. However, it is possible to add a duplicate (dup(2), dup2(2), fcntl(2) F_DUPFD) file descriptor to the same epoll instance. This can be a useful technique for filtering events, if the duplicate file descriptors are registered with different events masks.

facts.summary: dup, dup2, F_DUPFD and fork create new descriptors for the same open file description, and an entry leaves the interest list only after every descriptor for that description is closed.
facts.quote: Whenever a file descriptor is duplicated via dup(2), dup2(2), fcntl(2) F_DUPFD, or fork(2), a new file descriptor referring to the same open file description is created. … A file descriptor is removed from an interest list only after all the file descriptors referring to the underlying open file description have been closed.

facts.summary: After closing a registered fd, events may still be reported for it while other descriptors for the same description are open; the page says it must be removed with EPOLL_CTL_DEL before it is duplicated.
facts.quote: even after a file descriptor that is part of an interest list has been closed, events may be reported for that file descriptor if other file descriptors referring to the same underlying file description remain open. To prevent this happening, the file descriptor must be explicitly removed from the interest list (using epoll_ctl(2) EPOLL_CTL_DEL) before it is duplicated.

facts.summary: Several events occurring between two epoll_wait calls are combined, not reported separately.
facts.quote: If more than one event occurs between epoll_wait(2) calls, are they combined or reported separately? They will be combined.

facts.summary: A modify operation on a registered fd rereads the available I/O, affecting events collected but not yet reported.
facts.quote: Does an operation on a file descriptor affect the already collected but not yet reported events? … Modify will reread available I/O.

facts.summary: Answering whether ET needs read/write until EAGAIN, the page says a reported fd must be considered ready until the next nonblocking read or write yields EAGAIN.
facts.quote: Receiving an event from epoll_wait(2) should suggest to you that such file descriptor is ready for the requested I/O operation. You must consider it ready until the next (nonblocking) read/write yields EAGAIN.

facts.summary: For packet or token files the only way to detect exhaustion is to read/write until EAGAIN; for stream files a short read or write also shows it, but only if the fd is surely stream-oriented.
facts.quote: For packet/token-oriented files (e.g., datagram socket, terminal in canonical mode), the only way to detect the end of the read/write I/O space is to continue to read/write until EAGAIN. … For stream-oriented files (e.g., pipe, FIFO, stream socket), the condition that the read/write I/O space is exhausted can also be detected by checking the amount of data read from / written to the target file descriptor. … (Avoid this latter technique if you cannot guarantee that the monitored file descriptor always refers to a stream-oriented file.)

facts.summary: epoll(7) gives the API's history as Linux 2.5.44 and glibc 2.3.2.
facts.quote: Linux 2.5.44. glibc 2.3.2.

facts.summary: EPOLL_CTL_ADD adds an entry holding the fd, a reference to its open file description, and the given settings.
facts.quote: Add an entry to the interest list of the epoll file descriptor, epfd. The entry includes the file descriptor, fd, a reference to the corresponding open file description (see epoll(7) and open(2)), and the settings specified in event.

facts.summary: EPOLL_CTL_MOD replaces the settings of fd in the interest list with the new ones.
facts.quote: Change the settings associated with fd in the interest list to the new settings specified in event.

facts.summary: The events mask combines event types, which epoll_wait returns, with input flags, which change behaviour and are not returned.
facts.quote: The events member of the epoll_event structure is a bit mask composed by ORing together zero or more event types, returned by epoll_wait(2), and input flags, which affect its behavior, but aren't returned.

facts.summary: EPOLLRDHUP exists since Linux 2.6.17 and reports a stream peer closing or shutting down writing; the page calls it useful for edge-triggered monitoring.
facts.quote: EPOLLRDHUP (since Linux 2.6.17) Stream socket peer closed connection, or shut down writing half of connection. (This flag is especially useful for writing simple code to detect peer shutdown when using edge-triggered monitoring.)

facts.summary: EPOLLERR and EPOLLHUP are always reported by epoll_wait; the caller need not set them.
facts.quote: epoll_wait(2) will always report for this event; it is not necessary to set it in events when calling epoll_ctl(). EPOLLHUP Hang up happened on the associated file descriptor. epoll_wait(2) will always wait for this event; it is not necessary to set it in events when calling epoll_ctl().

facts.summary: EPOLLET is an input flag that requests edge-triggered notification; level-triggered is the default.
facts.quote: EPOLLET Requests edge-triggered notification for the associated file descriptor. The default behavior for epoll is level- triggered.

facts.summary: EPOLLONESHOT (since Linux 2.6.2): after one reported event the fd is disabled in the interest list, and the user must call EPOLL_CTL_MOD with a new mask to re-arm it.
facts.quote: EPOLLONESHOT (since Linux 2.6.2) Requests one-shot notification for the associated file descriptor. This means that after an event notified for the file descriptor by epoll_wait(2), the file descriptor is disabled in the interest list and no other events will be reported by the epoll interface. The user must call epoll_ctl() with EPOLL_CTL_MOD to rearm the file descriptor with a new event mask.

facts.summary: EPOLLWAKEUP (since Linux 3.5) keeps the system from suspending only if EPOLLONESHOT and EPOLLET are clear and the process has CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND.
facts.quote: EPOLLWAKEUP (since Linux 3.5) If EPOLLONESHOT and EPOLLET are clear and the process has the CAP_BLOCK_SUSPEND capability, ensure that the system does not enter "suspend" or "hibernate" while this event is pending or being processed.

facts.summary: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (since Linux 4.5): when several epoll fds watch one target file with this flag, one or more of them, not all, receive the event.
facts.quote: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE (since Linux 4.5) Sets an exclusive wakeup mode for the epoll file descriptor that is being attached to the target file descriptor, fd. When a wakeup event occurs and multiple epoll file descriptors are attached to the same target file using EPOLLEXCLUSIVE, one or more of the epoll file descriptors will receive an event with epoll_wait(2). The default in this scenario (when EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is not set) is for all epoll file descriptors to receive an event.

facts.summary: With a mix of exclusive and non-exclusive instances on one fd, all non-exclusive instances and at least one exclusive instance get the event.
facts.quote: If the same file descriptor is in multiple epoll instances, some with the EPOLLEXCLUSIVE flag, and others without, then events will be provided to all epoll instances that did not specify EPOLLEXCLUSIVE, and at least one of the epoll instances that did specify EPOLLEXCLUSIVE.

facts.summary: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE may be combined only with EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLWAKEUP and EPOLLET (EPOLLHUP and EPOLLERR optional); any other value, EPOLLONESHOT included, gives EINVAL.
facts.quote: The following values may be specified in conjunction with EPOLLEXCLUSIVE: EPOLLIN, EPOLLOUT, EPOLLWAKEUP, and EPOLLET. EPOLLHUP and EPOLLERR can also be specified, but this is not required: as usual, these events are always reported if they occur, regardless of whether they are specified in events. Attempts to specify other values in events yield the error EINVAL.

facts.summary: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE is allowed only with EPOLL_CTL_ADD; using it in EPOLL_CTL_MOD, a later EPOLL_CTL_MOD on an exclusive (epfd, fd) pair, or an epoll instance as target all fail with EINVAL.
facts.quote: EPOLLEXCLUSIVE may be used only in an EPOLL_CTL_ADD operation; attempts to employ it with EPOLL_CTL_MOD yield an error. If EPOLLEXCLUSIVE has been set using epoll_ctl(), then a subsequent EPOLL_CTL_MOD on the same epfd, fd pair yields an error. A call to epoll_ctl() that specifies EPOLLEXCLUSIVE in events and specifies the target file descriptor fd as an epoll instance will likewise fail. The error in all of these cases is EINVAL.

facts.summary: EPOLL_CTL_MOD on an fd not registered with the instance fails with ENOENT.
facts.quote: ENOENT op was EPOLL_CTL_MOD or EPOLL_CTL_DEL, and fd is not registered with this epoll instance.

facts.summary: epoll_ctl(2) gives the history as Linux 2.6 and glibc 2.3.2.
facts.quote: Linux 2.6, glibc 2.3.2.

facts.summary: epoll_wait returns, through the events buffer, information from the ready list about interest-list fds that have events.
facts.quote: is used to return information from the ready list about file descriptors in the interest list that have some events available.

facts.summary: The maximum-events argument must be greater than zero.
facts.quote: argument must be greater than zero.

facts.summary: epoll_wait blocks until a file descriptor delivers an event, a signal handler interrupts it, or the timeout expires.
facts.quote: will block until either: … a file descriptor delivers an event; … the call is interrupted by a signal handler; … the timeout expires.

facts.summary: A timeout of -1 blocks indefinitely; a timeout of 0 returns immediately even with no events.
facts.quote: of \-1 causes … to block indefinitely, while specifying a … equal to zero causes … to return immediately, even if no events are available.

facts.summary: The data field returned is the one given in the most recent EPOLL_CTL_ADD or EPOLL_CTL_MOD for that fd.
facts.quote: structure contains the same data as was specified in the most recent call to … for the corresponding open file descriptor.

facts.summary: The returned events field is a bit mask of the events that occurred for the open file description.
facts.quote: field is a bit mask that indicates the events that have occurred for the corresponding open file description.

facts.summary: On success epoll_wait returns the number of ready file descriptors, or zero when none became ready within the timeout.
facts.quote: returns the number of file descriptors ready for the requested I/O operation, or zero if no file descriptor became ready during the requested

facts.quote: Linux 2.6, … To be precise: Linux 2.5.44. … The interface should be finalized by Linux 2.5.66. … glibc 2.3.2. … Linux 2.6.19, … Linux 5.11.

facts.summary: Another thread may add an fd to an epoll instance while a thread is blocked in epoll_wait on it; if that fd becomes ready the blocked call returns.
facts.quote: it is possible for another thread to add a file descriptor to the waited-upon … If the new file descriptor becomes ready, it will cause the … call to unblock.

facts.summary: When more fds are ready than the buffer holds, successive epoll_wait calls round-robin through the ready set to avoid starvation.
facts.quote: If more than … file descriptors are ready when … is called, then successive … calls will round robin through the set of ready file descriptors. This behavior helps avoid starvation scenarios,

facts.summary: In v6.12, struct eventpoll holds rdllist, the list of ready file descriptors, and ovflist, a singly linked chain of epitems that became ready while events were being copied to user space without the lock.
facts.quote: /* List of ready file descriptors */ struct list_head rdllist; … This is a single linked list that chains all the "struct epitem" that happened while transferring ready events to userspace w/out holding ->lock. … struct epitem *ovflist;

facts.quote: struct epitem { … /* List header used to link this structure to the eventpoll ready list */ struct list_head rdllink;

facts.quote: EP_PRIVATE_BITS (EPOLLWAKEUP | EPOLLONESHOT | EPOLLET | EPOLLEXCLUSIVE)

facts.quote: EPOLLINOUT_BITS (EPOLLIN | EPOLLOUT) … EPOLLEXCLUSIVE_OK_BITS (EPOLLINOUT_BITS | EPOLLERR | EPOLLHUP | \ EPOLLWAKEUP | EPOLLET | EPOLLEXCLUSIVE)

This condition is likely the effect of the EPOLLONESHOT bit that disables the descriptor when an event is received, until the next EPOLL_CTL_MOD will be issued. … if (!(epi->event.events & ~EP_PRIVATE_BITS)) goto out_unlock;

facts.quote: If we are transferring events to userspace, we can hold no locks … All the events that happen during that period of time are chained in ep->ovflist and requeued later on. … if (READ_ONCE(ep->ovflist) != EP_UNACTIVE_PTR) { if (chain_epi_lockless(epi))

facts.quote: } else if (!ep_is_linked(epi)) { /* In the usual case, add event to ready list. */ if (list_add_tail_lockless(&epi->rdllink, &ep->rdllist))

facts.quote: if (epi->event.events & EPOLLEXCLUSIVE) add_wait_queue_exclusive(whead, &pwq->wait); else add_wait_queue(whead, &pwq->wait);

facts.quote: /* If the file is already "ready" we drop it inside the ready list */ if (revents && !ep_is_linked(epi)) { list_add_tail(&epi->rdllink, &ep->rdllist);

facts.summary: ep_send_events starts with ep_start_scan, which moves the whole ready list to a private list and sets ovflist to NULL so events arriving meanwhile are kept.
facts.quote: Steal the ready list, and re-init the original one to the empty list. Also, set ep->ovflist to NULL so that events happening while looping w/out locks, are not lost.

facts.quote: if (epi->event.events & EPOLLONESHOT) epi->event.events &= EP_PRIVATE_BITS;

conflicts.topic: which epoll_wait waiters are woken when an item becomes ready
conflicts.note: epoll(7) ties waking only one waiter to EPOLLET items; v6.12 source queues every epoll_wait waiter as exclusive in any mode, then re-queues level-triggered items and wakes another waiter in ep_done_scan.

conflicts.topic: does EPOLLWAKEUP apply together with EPOLLET
conflicts.note: epoll(7) describes EPOLLWAKEUP with no condition; epoll_ctl(2) says it applies only if EPOLLONESHOT and EPOLLET are clear.
epoll(7) says Linux 2.5.44, epoll_ctl(2) says Linux 2.6, epoll_wait(2) says 2.6 with a source comment giving 2.5.44 precisely and 2.5.66 for the final interface.
